::: {.panel-tabset}

### INTRODUCTION

::: {.two-col-side}

::: {}
![](utat_tank/images/problem.jpg)
:::

::: {}
- Analyzed and optimized the bulkheads and fuel tanks of UTAT's liquid propellent rocket
- Updated bulkheads to meet fluid volume requirements, selected O-rings, produced engineering drawings, and conducted FEA on final design
:::

:::

### PROCESS

::: {.two-col-cards}

::: {.step-card}
![](utat_tank/images/broken_bulkhead.png)

- Leads believed tank was engineered and would fail via bearing failure based on prior FEA
- Researched bolted joint analysis and performed hand calculations to determine stresses for each failure mode, including bolt tear out, casing tensile failure, bolt shear failure, and bearing failure
:::

::: {.step-card}
![](utat_tank/images/broken_bolts.png)

- Contrary to prior belief, calculations showed that the tank was overengineered with a safety factor of 3, and that bolt shear was the actual governing failure mode
- Validated analysis via hydrostatic burst testing; tank withstood >2.5x design pressure and failed via bolt shear as predicted
:::

:::

::: {.two-col-cards}

::: {.step-card}
![](utat_tank/images/bulkhead_cad.png)

- Reduced factor of safety to 1.75 by decreasing tank wall thickness by 33% and bolt count by 20%
- Implemented shoulder bolts to improve tank resistance to bolt shear failure
- Redesigned bulkheads with Onshape for updated fluid volumes and produced engineering drawings
:::

::: {.step-card}
![](utat_tank/images/drawing.png)

- Selected temperature- and chemical-compatible O-rings
- Implemented groove dimensions and tolerances to match Parker handbook recommendations for proper sealing
:::

:::

::: {.two-image-row}

::: {}
![](utat_tank/images/bulkhead_fea.png)
:::

::: {}
![](utat_tank/images/downcomer_fea.png)
:::

:::

- Conducted FEA with ANSYS on final bulkheads and downcomer tube
- Calculated worst-case thermal deformation of fuel tank walls to resolve Launch Canada's concern that downcomer would fail due to thermal contraction, showing a safety factor in excess of 3.5

### RESULTS

- Fuel tank wall thickness reduced by 33% and bolt count by 20%
- Maintained a safety factor >1.5 on all components for a 1000 psi maximum expected operating pressure
- Resolved Launch Canada's concerns regarding the downcomer, allowing retention of existing design

:::
